html:
Ai-Khanoum was a Greek city on the Oxus river, the Amu Darya, in what is now northern Afghanistan. It was founded around 280 BCE and is the easternmost Greek city ever dug up.

It was built under the Seleucids, heirs of Alexander the Great, and became a great city of the Greco-Bactrian kingdom. It stood where the Kokcha river joins the Oxus, on the route of the lapis lazuli and gold of the mountains.

French archaeologists excavated it from 1964 to 1978. They found a Greek world far from Greece:

  • a theatre for about 6,000 people and a large gymnasium
  • a vast palace mixing Greek and Persian styles
  • Greek inscriptions, among them moral sayings copied from Delphi by a traveller named Clearchus

Around 145 BCE the city was sacked and burned, probably by nomads from the north such as the Yuezhi, and never rebuilt. During the Afghan wars after 1979 the site was heavily looted, and much of what the excavators left is gone.
sum: Ai-Khanoum was a Greek city on the Oxus river, the Amu Darya, in what is now northern Afghanistan. It was founded around 280 BCE and is the easternmost Greek city ever dug up.
